title: Clamp auto-expand replicas to the closest value

timeline.body:
Ensure that the number of replicas chosen for an auto-expand-able index
is within the range of the available data nodes, i.e., excluding those
nodes that cannot be assigned a replica.

Closes #84788

timeline.message:
Clamp auto-expand replicas to the closest value

Ensure that the number of replicas chosen for an auto-expand-able shard
is within the range of the available data nodes, i.e., excluding those
nodes that cannot be assigned a replica.

Closes #84788
timeline.author: Pooya Salehi

timeline.body:
I was wondering if it is a good idea to test a private method/logic. I think having a small test like `testCalculateDesiredNumberOfReplica` justifies exposing this otherwise private logic, since the test makes it clear what is expected when calculating replicas. 

I went with package-private since the other alternative of using protected doesn't make much sense considering this is a record class.

reply.body: Yes, that is fine, we do that often.

+    /**
+     * Verifies that when no data node is available to host a replica, number of replicas are contracted to 0.
+     */
+    public void testAutoExpandToClosesValue() throws Exception {
+        final String indexName = "myindex";
+        final String autoExpandValue = randomFrom("0-1", "0-all");
+        createIndex(
+            indexName,
+            Settings.builder()
+                .put(IndexMetadata.SETTING_NUMBER_OF_SHARDS, 1)
+                .put(IndexMetadata.SETTING_AUTO_EXPAND_REPLICAS, autoExpandValue)
+                .build()
+        );
+
+        final int initialReplicas = autoExpandValue.equals("0-1") ? 1 : internalCluster().numDataNodes() - 1;
+
+        assertBusy(() -> {
+            assertThat(
+                client().admin()
+                    .indices()
+                    .prepareGetSettings(indexName)
+                    .setNames("index.number_of_replicas")
+                    .get()
+                    .getSetting(indexName, "index.number_of_replicas"),
+                equalTo(String.valueOf(initialReplicas))
+            );
+        });
+        ensureGreen(indexName);

reply.body: IMO, at least for the sake of making it clear what the test expects, we should leave it here. Removing it didn't seem to really speedup the test.

It is not about test speed. But waiting for green here signals that it is important to the test. But the test will pass without this, since our auto-expand calculation is independent of the status of the index. Hence I think we should simply remove it.

timeline.body: Can we also remove the setting and see that it jumps back to the `initialReplicas` value, thus checking that it clamps to the higher bound too?
The `Math.min` done in `getMaxReplicas` seems redundant now, I think we should remove it, it is somewhat confusing now.

reply.body: That's a very good point! It also simplifies the code and the parsing test. Done in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/87505/commits/ec7d7f97bc039f46d8c508943783b44ea78edae2.
